added_records.title: Objective Sleep Quality Prediction from the Period Before Sleep Onset
added_records.abstract: Insufficient sleep is associated with cognitive decline, metabolic issues, and mood disorders. Yet evaluations of sleep quality often depend on subjective reports and lack adaptive tools for personalized intervention. We analyzed EEG from 197 Sleep-EDF participants and predicted deep_sleep percentage (N3%) using features extracted solely from a 5–15 minute pre-sleep window. Inputs included age, sex, band powers, alpha peak, and 1/f slope. Four machine learning regressors—LR, SVR, RF, and XGBoost—were trained with nested 10-fold crossvalidation. RF and XGBoost outperformed LR and SVR. XGBoost achieved Pearson 0.86–0.89, MAE 1.62–1.96%, and RMSE 4.14–4.55%. Longer pre-sleep windows improved performance slightly. Alpha peak and 1/f slope were the strongest EEG predictors besides age and sex. These results show that short pre-sleep EEG fragments carry predictive information about sleep quality measured by N3%.

added_records.title: AdWave: Adaptive Wavelet Attention with Multi-Scale Fusion for Noise-Robust OCT Segmentation
added_records.abstract: In ophthalmic clinical practice, accurate segmentation of anatomical layers and pathological lesions in Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is essential for identifying structural abnormalities. However, the inherent speckle noise in OCT images introduces stochastic intensity variations that obscure fine-grained structural details and degrade segmentation accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose Ad-Wave, a novel segmentation framework that adaptively enhances structural discriminability and suppresses speckle interference through frequency-spatial collaborative learning. Specifically, we introduce an Adaptive Wavelet Attention (AWA) module that selectively attenuates noise-sensitive high-frequency components, while enhancing relevant structural cues that guide the model's attention to target regions; and a Multi-scale Dual-domain Fusion Skip Connection (MDF) that aggregates complementary frequency and spatial features across scales to reduce boundary ambiguity and improve contextual understanding. Comprehensive evaluations on GOALS (healthy/glaucoma) and DUKEBOE (diabetic macular edema) datasets validate AdWave's effectiveness. The results demonstrated superior performance in retinal layer and lesion segmentation, along with strong robustness under speckle noise interference. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhangHH233/AdWave.

added_records.title: FINE-Net: A Frequency-Integrated Hybrid Framework for Interpretable Motor Imagery EEG Decoding
added_records.abstract: Brain–computer interface (BCI) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, providing new opportunities for functional recovery in individuals with motor impairments. Among various approaches, decoding electroencephalogram (EEG) signals based on motor imagery (MI) has emerged as a key research direction. Although deep learning methods outperform traditional machine learning approaches in terms of decoding accuracy, their practical application remains limited by poor interpretability and feature redundancy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel hybrid network architecture that integrates traditional feature extraction techniques with deep learning. The deep learning module adopts a parallel multibranch design: one branch processes raw EEG signals using lightweight and interpretable convolutional structures to capture frequency-specific features, while the other encodes spatial information from EEG signals filtered by multiple band-pass filters and leverages an attention mechanism to supply complementary frequency information to the primary branch. Experimental results on the BCI4-2A and BCI4-2B datasets demonstrate average accuracies of 89.81% and 85.63%, respectively. In addition, this work fuses traditional handcrafted features with deep learning-based representations, and proposes a feature selection strategy based on distance correlation to identify informative and complementary feature subsets. The final hybrid network architecture achieves improved average accuracies of 93.43% and 86.69% on the two datasets, while exhibiting enhanced robustness and interpretability. This design effectively balances decoding performance and model explainability.

added_records.title: Collaborative Pseudo-Label Refinement Between Conventional and Foundation Models for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
added_records.abstract: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation relies heavily on the quality of pseudo-labels. Conventional segmentation networks capture semantic regions while struggling with precise boundaries, whereas the class-agnostic Segment Anything Model (SAM) yields sharp edges but lacks medical semantic priors due to natural-image pre-training. To leverage their complementary strengths, we propose a collaborative pseudolabel refinement framework that integrates conventional and foundation models. Specifically, conventional model predictions are used to generate point prompts for SAM, which produces boundary-enhanced segmentations that refine pseudo-labels in uncertain regions. Our framework is built upon a Structural Rectification Network (SRN) with two modules: the Dynamic Prompt Fusion Core (DPFC) for low-uncertainty prompt fusion, and the Cross-model Discrepancy Exploiter (CDE) for dualstudent co-optimization. Extensive experiments conducted on two widely used benchmarks show the effectiveness of our method, achieving notable Dice improvements.

added_records.title: PFed-Signal: An ADR Prediction Model Based on Federated Learning
added_records.abstract: The adverse drug reactions (ADRs) predicted based on the biased records in FAERS (U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System) may mislead diagnosis online. Generally, such problems are solved by optimizing reporting odds ratio (ROR) or proportional reporting ratio (PRR). However, these methods that rely on statistical methods cannot eliminate the biased data, leading to inaccurate signal prediction. In this paper, we propose PFed-signal, a federated learning-based signal prediction model of ADR, which utilizes the Euclidean distance to eliminate the biased data from FAERS, thereby improving the accuracy of ADR prediction. Specifically, we first propose Pfed-Split, a method to split the original dataset into a split dataset based on ADR. Then we propose ADR-signal, an ADR prediction model, including a biased data identification method based on federated learning and an ADR prediction model based on Transformer. The former identifies the biased data according to the Euclidean distance and generates a clean dataset by deleting the biased data. added_records.abstract: This paper proposes a machine learning framework that utilizes the dynamics of the pupillary light reflex (PLR) to achieve non-invasive identification of substance abusers. We constructed a clinical pupillary dataset comprising 1,063 subjects (523 substance abusers and 540 healthy controls). Forty-four multidimensional metrics, including statistical, dynamic response, frequency domain, morphological, and nonlinear features, were extracted from a 125-frame sequence of PLR diameter changes; subsequently, 41 key biomarkers with clinical interpretability were retained following screening. To achieve high-performance classification, we designed a CV-Weighted Heterogeneous SoftVoting Ensemble based on Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimization that integrates five representative base classifiers: Gaussian Process, Extra Trees, CatBoost, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and AdaBoost. The decision-making mechanism uses dynamic weighted voting. Regarding model interpretation, SHAP value analysis and Pearson correlation heat maps elucidate the intrinsic relationship between model discriminants and features. The final model attained 84.04 % accuracy and 90.23 % AUC on the independent test set, demonstrating exceptional recognition performance. The primary frequency peak (freq_peak1) and pupil diameter variability (std) are the two most significant features, collectively accounting for 56.7 % of the total feature importance. This study developed a GA-driven heterogeneous integrated recognition framework based on PLR dynamics, enhancing clinical interpretability while facilitating rapid and non-invasive drug abuse screening. The proposed method provides quantitative biological insights into autonomic dysfunction induced by addictive drugs and presents extensive application prospects for public health surveillance and clinically assisted decision-making.

11356311.abstract: Multimodal survival prediction combining genomic features with histopathology whole slide images (WSIs) has shown promise, but genomic data remains costly and inaccessible for widespread clinical adoption. In contrast, clinical data and multi-stained WSIs are routinely available. We present Contrastive Learning guided by Pathological Reports (CLPR), a multimodal survival prediction framework that integrates H&Estained WSIs, immunohistochemical (IHC)-stained WSIs, and structured pathological reports. Unlike genomic approaches, IHC provides protein-level tumor microenvironment information at lower cost, while pathological reports bridge clinical diagnosis with prognostic assessment. CLPR addresses key challenges in multimodal fusion through three innovations: (1) pathological report-guided contrastive learning that identifies semantically meaningful sample pairs for robust cross-modal alignment, overcoming unreliable attention scores under weak supervision; (2) a distribution-aware regularization constraint that explicitly preserves inter-group separability and intra-group compactness between risk cohorts, enhancing discriminative power; and (3) the first multimodal survival dataset combining H&E- and IHC-stained WSIs with structured pathological reports. On our clinical gastric cancer dataset (270 patients), CLPR achieves a C-index of 0.785 with significant risk stratification (log-rank p < 1e-5), outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Notably, CLPR maintains strong performance even without IHC data (C-index: 0.772), demonstrating clinical versatility.

Abstract:
Diabetes self-management continues to exhibit wide interpersonal variability, a phenomenon insufficiently addressed by standardized Diabetes Self-Management Education (DSME) programs. The limitations of existing approaches stem largely from their implicit assumption of homogeneous cognitive structures, an assumption inconsistent with theoretical insights from conceptual metaphor theory and cognitive science indicating that individuals rely on divergent conceptual mappings to make sense of chronic illness. This study addresses this gap by conducting a large-scale computational analysis of 39,880 spontaneous patient self-disclosures from diabetes-related subreddits using MetaPro to uncover the underlying cognitive frameworks of diabetic patients. Comparative analysis demonstrated significant differences in cognitive conceptualizations between type 1 (T1D) and type 2 (T2D) diabetes patients. T1D discourse is dominated by an “action-monitoring” schema, whereas T2D discourse emphasizes a “process-mishap-component” schema. Gender comparisons further distinguish a male “metric-status-trajectory” profile from a female “burden-care-intuition” profile. These findings illuminate the deep cognitive heterogeneity underlying diabetes self-management and underscore the need for personalized, cognitively informed intervention strategies that attend to demographic and clinical distinctions.

abstract.abstract: Establishing an objective and quantifiable analysis of the behaviors of children with autism remains a major challenge in current research. Behavioral analysis is essential for both early autism screening and designing effective intervention strategies. Drawing on theories from psychology and behavioral science, we propose an explainable interactive digital behavioral analysis method grounded in spatial correlation. Using a series of context-based behavioral stimulation paradigms, we collected multi-modal reactive behaviors from 112 children. We then compared the response patterns of children with autism to their clinically observed symptoms to evaluate the developmental status of the core competencies underlying their behaviors. By quantifying children's multi-modal responses through a spatial correlation behavioral paradigm analysis method, we generated digital behavioral representations and applied them to autism screening, achieving an accuracy of 94.4 %. These results validate the effectiveness and reliability of our digital behavioral analysis approach, demonstrating its potential value in supporting objective autism screening and informing subsequent intervention planning.

By quantifying children's multi-modal responses through a spatial correlation behavioral paradigm analysis method, we generated digital behavioral representations and applied them to autism screening, achieving an accuracy of 94.4 %.   - paragraph:
    - text: "Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by poor social communication skills, repetitive behaviors, and narrow interests [1], , [3]. According to global reports, the overall prevalence of autism has increased from 0.62 % in 2012 to 1 % in 2022[4]. Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) require extensive support from educational, medical, and social systems, resulting in a significant economic burden. Furthermore, disability has spillover effects that diminish the quality of life of the entire family [5]. Research has shown that analyzing the behavior of children with autism, conducting early screening, and designing targeted intervention plans can effectively improve their behavior in the later stages [6], , [8]. Given that ASD cannot currently be objectively measured through any biological or medical tests or technologies, behavioral assessment is the only available diagnostic tool. However, current assessments of the behavior of children with ASD are primarily based on scales such as the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) and the Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC), which are susceptible to issues related to the doctor's subjectivity and interpretive biases. With the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital behavioral analysis methods for children with autism are increasingly being applied to autism screening. Increasingly, researchers are using Computer Vision (CV) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies to collect and analyze physiological characteristics, such as eye movements, in children, thus facilitating a more objective autism screening process [9]. However, as autism is a spectrum disorder, its symptoms inevitably manifest differently in different individuals. Analyzing children's behavior solely by quantifying the behavioral heterogeneity between ASD children and Typically Developing (TD) children is too one-sided. In response to the current lack of research, we propose the following two contributions:"

Using a series of context-based behavioral stimulation paradigms, we collected multi-modal reactive behaviors from 112 children. We then compared the response patterns of children with autism to their clinically observed symptoms to evaluate the developmental status of the core competencies underlying their behaviors. By quantifying children's multi-modal responses through a spatial correlation behavioral paradigm analysis method, we generated digital behavioral representations and applied them to autism screening, achieving an accuracy of 94.4 %. These results validate the effectiveness and reliability of our digital behavioral analysis approach, demonstrating its potential value in supporting objective autism screening and informing subsequent intervention planning.

Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) require extensive support from educational, medical, and social systems, resulting in a significant economic burden. Furthermore, disability has spillover effects that diminish the quality of life of the entire family [5]. Research has shown that analyzing the behavior of children with autism, conducting early screening, and designing targeted intervention plans can effectively improve their behavior in the later stages [6], , [8]. Given that ASD cannot currently be objectively measured through any biological or medical tests or technologies, behavioral assessment is the only available diagnostic tool. However, current assessments of the behavior of children with ASD are primarily based on scales such as the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) and the Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC), which are susceptible to issues related to the doctor's subjectivity and interpretive biases. Increasingly, researchers are using Computer Vision (CV) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies to collect and analyze physiological characteristics, such as eye movements, in children, thus facilitating a more objective autism screening process [9].
